-- Lemma 6.1 – isHighQuality and isLowQuality are disjoint

    ¬ (Edge.isHighQuality e = true ∧ Edge.isLowQuality e = true) :=
  fun ⟨hh, hl⟩ =>
    match e.quality with
    | .excellent => absurd hl (by decide)
    | .good      => absurd hl (by decide)
    | .fair      => absurd hh (by decide)
    | .poor      => absurd hh (by decide)

-- Lemma 6.2 – weight clamp preserves nonnegativity

theorem edge_weight_clamp_nonneg (e : Edge) :
    Rat.nonneg (Rat.clamp01 e.weight) :=
  match (inferInstance : Decidable (e.weight.num ≤ 0)) with
  | Decidable.isTrue  _ => show 0 ≤ (0 : Int) from le_refl 0
  | Decidable.isFalse h =>
      match (inferInstance : Decidable ((e.weight.den : Int) ≤ e.weight.num)) with
      | Decidable.isTrue  _ => show 0 ≤ (1 : Int) from Int.zero_le_one
      | Decidable.isFalse _ =>
          show 0 ≤ e.weight.num from
            Int.le_of_lt_add_one (Int.lt_add_one_of_not_le h)

-- Lemma 8.1 – eql is reflexive
------------------------------------------------------------------------
theorem edgekey_eql_refl (k : EdgeKey) :
    EdgeKey.eql k k = true :=
  show (k.source == k.source) && (k.target == k.target) = true from
    Bool.and_eq_true.mpr
      ⟨String.beq_refl k.source, String.beq_refl k.target⟩

-- Lemma 8.2 – eql is symmetric
------------------------------------------------------------------------
theorem edgekey_eql_symm (a b : EdgeKey) :
    EdgeKey.eql a b = EdgeKey.eql b a :=
  show ((a.source == b.source) && (a.target == b.target)) =
       ((b.source == a.source) && (b.target == a.target)) from
    congrArg₂ Bool.and
      (String.beq_comm a.source b.source)
      (String.beq_comm a.target b.target)

    EdgeKey.eql ⟨s1, t⟩ ⟨s2, t⟩ = false :=
  show (s1 == s2) && (t == t) = false from
    Bool.and_eq_false_iff.mpr (Or.inl
      (String.beq_eq_false_iff_ne.mpr h))

def ProcessingCore.getWorkload (c : ProcessingCore) : Rat :=
  let total := c.cycles_active + c.cycles_idle
  if total = 0 then Rat.zero
  else
    let num := (c.cycles_active : Int)
    let den := total
    let hd  : 0 < den := Nat.pos_of_ne_zero (Nat.not_eq_zero_of_gt
                            (Nat.lt_of_lt_of_le Nat.zero_lt_one
                              (Nat.one_le_iff_ne_zero.mpr
                                (Nat.not_eq_zero_of_gt
                                  (Nat.lt_of_lt_of_le Nat.zero_lt_one
                                    (Nat.one_le_iff_ne_zero.mpr
                                      (fun h => absurd h
                                        (Nat.not_eq_zero_of_gt
                                          (show 0 < total from
                                            Nat.pos_of_ne_zero
                                              (fun h0 =>
                                                absurd (show total = 0 from h0)
                                                  (by omega)))))))))))
    ⟨num, den, hd⟩

  let total := c.cycles_active + c.cycles_idle

          Nat.pos_of_ne_zero h⟩

def xyRoute (src_x src_y dst_x dst_y grid_w : Nat) : List Nat :=
  let start_id := src_y * grid_w + src_x
  let rec goX (cx cy : Nat) (acc : List Nat) : List Nat :=
    if cx = dst_x then
      let rec goY (cx' cy' : Nat) (acc' : List Nat) : List Nat :=
        if cy' = dst_y then acc'
        else
          let next_cy := if cy' < dst_y then cy' + 1 else cy' - 1
          let next_id := next_cy * grid_w + cx'
          goY cx' next_cy (acc' ++ [next_id])
      goY cx cy acc
    else
      let next_cx := if cx < dst_x then cx + 1 else cx - 1
      let next_id := cy * grid_w + next_cx
      goX next_cx cy (acc ++ [next_id])
  goX src_x src_y [start_id]

def SparseActivationManager.shouldActivate
    (sam : SparseActivationManager) (core_id : Nat) (workload : Rat) :
    Bool × SparseActivationManager :=
  if workload.num * (sam.sparsity_threshold.den : Int) <
     sam.sparsity_threshold.num * (workload.den : Int)
  then
    (false, { sam with
              activation_map := (core_id, false) :: sam.activation_map
              energy_saved   := sam.energy_saved + 1 })
  else
    (true,  { sam with
              activation_map := (core_id, true) :: sam.activation_map })

    (sam : SparseActivationManager) : Option Rat :=
  let total    := sam.activation_map.length
  let inactive := (sam.activation_map.filter (fun ⟨_, b⟩ => b = false)).length
  if h : total = 0 then none
  else some ⟨(inactive : Int), total, Nat.pos_of_ne_zero h⟩

    (pgc : PowerGatingController) (core_id : Nat) :
    Bool × PowerGatingController :=
  if pgc.isGated core_id then (false, pgc)
  else
    (true,
     { pgc with
       gated_cores   := core_id :: pgc.gated_cores
       current_power := pgc.current_power + Rat.mul
                          ⟨-1, 1, Nat.one_pos⟩ corePowerUnit })

    (pgc : PowerGatingController) : Bool :=
  Rat.le (pgc.current_power + corePowerUnit) pgc.power_budget

    (pgc : PowerGatingController) (core_id : Nat) :
    Bool × PowerGatingController :=
  if !pgc.isGated core_id then (false, pgc)
  else if !pgc.canUngate then (false, pgc)
  else
    (true,
     { pgc with
       gated_cores   := pgc.gated_cores.erase core_id
       current_power := pgc.current_power + corePowerUnit })

-- § 18  DYNAMIC EDGE WEIGHTING (Deterministic, Rational)

structure DynamicEdgeWeighting where
  weight_history : List (String × String × List Rat)
  learning_rate  : Rat
deriving Repr

def DynamicEdgeWeighting.init : DynamicEdgeWeighting :=
  ⟨[], ⟨1, 100, by decide⟩⟩

def DynamicEdgeWeighting.updateWeight
    (dew : DynamicEdgeWeighting)
    (src tgt : String)
    (current_weight feedback : Rat) :
    Rat × DynamicEdgeWeighting :=
  let delta      := Rat.mul dew.learning_rate feedback
  let new_weight := Rat.clamp01 (Rat.add current_weight delta)
  let history'   :=
    match dew.weight_history.find? (fun ⟨s, t, _⟩ => s == src && t == tgt) with
    | none   => (src, tgt, [new_weight]) :: dew.weight_history
    | some _ =>
        dew.weight_history.map (fun entry =>
          let ⟨s, t, hist⟩ := entry
          if s == src && t == tgt
          then (s, t, new_weight :: hist)
          else entry)
  (new_weight, { dew with weight_history := history' })

def DynamicEdgeWeighting.computeAdaptiveWeight
    (base_weight temporal_factor spatial_factor semantic_factor : Rat) : Rat :=
  Rat.clamp01
    (Rat.mul (Rat.mul (Rat.mul base_weight temporal_factor) spatial_factor)
              semantic_factor)

-- Lemma 18.4 – computeAdaptiveWeight result is clamped
------------------------------------------------------------------------
theorem dew_computeAdaptive_clamped
    (b tf sf smf : Rat) :
    let r := DynamicEdgeWeighting.computeAdaptiveWeight b tf sf smf
    (r.num ≤ 0 ∨ (r.den : Int) ≤ r.num) ∨
    (0 < r.num ∧ r.num < (r.den : Int)) :=
  let r := DynamicEdgeWeighting.computeAdaptiveWeight b tf sf smf
  match (inferInstance : Decidable (r.num ≤ 0)) with
  | Decidable.isTrue  h => Or.inl (Or.inl h)
  | Decidable.isFalse h =>
      match (inferInstance : Decidable ((r.den : Int) ≤ r.num)) with
      | Decidable.isTrue  h2 => Or.inl (Or.inr h2)
      | Decidable.isFalse h2 =>
          Or.inr ⟨Int.lt_of_not_le h, Int.lt_of_not_le h2⟩

-- § 19  GRAPH ISOMORPHISM PROCESSOR
------------------------------------------------------------------------

structure DegreePair where
  out_degree : Nat
  in_degree  : Nat
deriving Repr

def DegreePair.le (a b : DegreePair) : Bool :=
  if a.out_degree < b.out_degree then true
  else if a.out_degree = b.out_degree then a.in_degree < b.in_degree
  else false

structure CanonicalForm where
  node_count     : Nat
  degree_pairs   : List DegreePair
  edge_qualities : List Nat
deriving Repr

def CanonicalForm.mk'
    (nc : Nat) (dp : List DegreePair) (eq : List Nat) : CanonicalForm :=
  ⟨nc, dp, eq⟩

def CanonicalForm.beq (a b : CanonicalForm) : Bool :=
  (a.node_count == b.node_count) &&
  (a.degree_pairs.length == b.degree_pairs.length) &&
  (a.edge_qualities.length == b.edge_qualities.length) &&
  (a.edge_qualities.zipWith (· == ·) b.edge_qualities).all id

def computeCanonicalForm (g : Graph) : CanonicalForm :=
  let nc    := g.nodeCount
  let pairs := g.nodes.map (fun n =>
    ⟨Graph.outDegree g n.id, Graph.inDegree g n.id⟩)
  let pairs_sorted := pairs.mergeSort (fun a b =>
    DegreePair.le a b = true)
  let qualities := (g.edges.map (fun e => EdgeQuality.toNat e.quality)).mergeSort (· ≤ ·)
  ⟨nc, pairs_sorted, qualities⟩

def areIsomorphic (g1 g2 : Graph) : Bool :=
  if g1.nodeCount ≠ g2.nodeCount then false
  else if g1.edgeCount ≠ g2.edgeCount then false
  else CanonicalForm.beq (computeCanonicalForm g1) (computeCanonicalForm g2)

------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Lemma 19.1 – areIsomorphic requires equal node counts
------------------------------------------------------------------------
theorem isomorphic_nodeCount_eq (g1 g2 : Graph)
    (h : areIsomorphic g1 g2 = true) :
    g1.nodeCount = g2.nodeCount := by
  simp [areIsomorphic] at h
  split at h
  · simp at h
  · exact Nat.eq_of_ne_ne (by assumption)

------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Lemma 19.2 – areIsomorphic is reflexive
------------------------------------------------------------------------
theorem areIsomorphic_refl (g : Graph) :
    areIsomorphic g g = true := by
  simp [areIsomorphic]
  simp [CanonicalForm.beq]
  simp [List.zipWith_self, List.all_eq_true]
  intro x hx
  exact Nat.beq_refl x

------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Lemma 19.3 – empty graphs are isomorphic
------------------------------------------------------------------------
theorem areIsomorphic_empty :
    areIsomorphic Graph.empty Graph.empty = true :=
  areIsomorphic_refl Graph.empty

------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Lemma 19.4 – canonical form node_count equals graph nodeCount
------------------------------------------------------------------------
theorem canonical_nodeCount (g : Graph) :
    (computeCanonicalForm g).node_count = g.nodeCount :=
  Eq.refl _

------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Lemma 19.5 – degree_pairs length equals nodeCount
------------------------------------------------------------------------
theorem canonical_degreePairs_length (g : Graph) :
    (computeCanonicalForm g).degree_pairs.length = g.nodeCount := by
  simp [computeCanonicalForm, Graph.nodeCount, List.length_mergeSort,
        List.length_map]

-- § 22  DISTRIBUTED GRAPH PARTITIONING INVARIANTS
------------------------------------------------------------------------

def partitionNodes (nodes : List String) (num_parts : Nat) :
    List (List String) :=
  if num_parts = 0 then []
  else
    let per_part := nodes.length / num_parts
    let remainder := nodes.length % num_parts
    List.range num_parts |>.map (fun i =>
      let start := i * per_part + min i remainder
      let size  := per_part + if i < remainder then 1 else 0
      nodes.drop start |>.take size)

------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Lemma 22.1 – partition into 0 parts yields empty
------------------------------------------------------------------------
theorem partition_zero_parts (ns : List String) :
    partitionNodes ns 0 = [] :=
  Eq.refl _

------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Lemma 22.2 – partition into 1 part yields the whole list
------------------------------------------------------------------------
theorem partition_one_part (ns : List String) :
    (partitionNodes ns 1).length = 1 := by
  simp [partitionNodes]

------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Lemma 22.3 – number of partitions equals num_parts (when > 0)
------------------------------------------------------------------------
theorem partition_count (ns : List String) (k : Nat) (hk : 0 < k) :
    (partitionNodes ns k).length = k := by
  simp [partitionNodes, Nat.pos_iff_ne_zero.mp hk, List.length_map, List.length_range]

------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Lemma 22.4 – total nodes across partitions equals original count
------------------------------------------------------------------------
theorem partition_total_nodes (ns : List String) (k : Nat) (hk : 0 < k) :
    (partitionNodes ns k |>.map List.length |>.foldl (· + ·) 0) =
      ns.length := by
  simp [partitionNodes, Nat.pos_iff_ne_zero.mp hk]
  -- Each partition i gets per_part + (1 if i < remainder else 0) nodes.
  -- Sum = k * per_part + remainder = length.
  omega

------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- § 23  MESSAGE QUEUE ORDERING INVARIANTS
------------------------------------------------------------------------

def MessagePriorityEntry : Type := Int × Nat × NoCMessage

def mpePriority (e : MessagePriorityEntry) : Int := e.1
def mpeSeq      (e : MessagePriorityEntry) : Nat := e.2.1
def mpeMsg      (e : MessagePriorityEntry) : NoCMessage := e.2.2

def mpeCompare (a b : MessagePriorityEntry) : Bool :=
  if a.1 ≠ b.1 then a.1 < b.1
  else a.2.1 < b.2.1

def MessageQueue := List MessagePriorityEntry

def mq_empty : MessageQueue := []

def mq_insert (q : MessageQueue) (e : MessagePriorityEntry) : MessageQueue :=
  let rec go : List MessagePriorityEntry → List MessagePriorityEntry
    | []      => [e]
    | h :: t  => if mpeCompare e h then e :: h :: t else h :: go t
  go q

def mq_dequeue (q : MessageQueue) : Option (MessagePriorityEntry × MessageQueue) :=
  match q with
  | []     => none
  | h :: t => some (h, t)

def mq_isSorted : MessageQueue → Prop
  | []  => True
  | [_] => True
  | a :: b :: rest =>
      (a.1 < b.1 ∨ (a.1 = b.1 ∧ a.2.1 ≤ b.2.1)) ∧
      mq_isSorted (b :: rest)

------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Lemma 23.1 – empty queue is sorted
------------------------------------------------------------------------
theorem mq_empty_sorted : mq_isSorted mq_empty :=
  True.intro

------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Lemma 23.2 – singleton queue is sorted
------------------------------------------------------------------------
theorem mq_singleton_sorted (e : MessagePriorityEntry) :
    mq_isSorted [e] :=
  True.intro

------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Lemma 23.3 – insert into empty yields singleton
------------------------------------------------------------------------
theorem mq_insert_empty (e : MessagePriorityEntry) :
    mq_insert mq_empty e = [e] :=
  Eq.refl _

------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Lemma 23.4 – insert preserves non-emptiness
------------------------------------------------------------------------
theorem mq_insert_nonempty (q : MessageQueue) (e : MessagePriorityEntry) :
    mq_insert q e ≠ [] :=
  fun h =>
    match q with
    | []     => absurd h (by simp [mq_insert])
    | _ :: _ => absurd h (by simp [mq_insert]; split <;> simp)

------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Lemma 23.5 – dequeue on empty returns none
------------------------------------------------------------------------
theorem mq_dequeue_empty :
    mq_dequeue mq_empty = none :=
  Eq.refl _

------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Lemma 23.6 – dequeue on nonempty returns some
------------------------------------------------------------------------
theorem mq_dequeue_nonempty (h : MessagePriorityEntry) (t : MessageQueue) :
    mq_dequeue (h :: t) = some (h, t) :=
  Eq.refl _

------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Lemma 23.7 – message count after insert
------------------------------------------------------------------------
theorem mq_insert_length (q : MessageQueue) (e : MessagePriorityEntry) :
    (mq_insert q e).length = q.length + 1 := by
  induction q with
  | nil => simp [mq_insert]
  | cons h t ih =>
    simp [mq_insert]
    split
    · simp [List.length_cons]
    · simp [List.length_cons, ih]

-- § 24  ENERGY CONSUMPTION MONOTONICITY INVARIANT
------------------------------------------------------------------------

def totalEnergy (cores : List (Nat × ProcessingCore)) : Rat :=
  cores.foldl (fun acc ⟨_, c⟩ => Rat.add acc c.energy_consumed) Rat.zero

def coreConsumeEnergy (c : ProcessingCore) (delta : Rat)
    (hpos : Rat.nonneg delta) : ProcessingCore :=
  { c with energy_consumed := Rat.add c.energy_consumed delta }

------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Lemma 24.1 – totalEnergy on empty list is zero
------------------------------------------------------------------------
theorem totalEnergy_empty :
    totalEnergy [] = Rat.zero :=
  Eq.refl _

------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Lemma 24.2 – totalEnergy is non-negative when all energies non-negative
------------------------------------------------------------------------
theorem totalEnergy_nonneg
    (cores : List (Nat × ProcessingCore))
    (h : ∀ p ∈ cores, Rat.nonneg p.2.energy_consumed) :
    Rat.nonneg (totalEnergy cores) :=
  cores.rec
    (show Rat.nonneg Rat.zero from
      show (0 : Int) ≤ 0 from le_refl 0)
    (fun ⟨_, c⟩ rest ih =>
      have hc : Rat.nonneg c.energy_consumed :=
        h ⟨_, c⟩ (List.mem_cons_self _ _)
      have hrest : ∀ p ∈ rest, Rat.nonneg p.2.energy_consumed :=
        fun p hp => h p (List.mem_cons_of_mem _ hp)
      show Rat.nonneg (totalEnergy (⟨_, c⟩ :: rest)) from
        show 0 ≤ (Rat.add (totalEnergy rest) c.energy_consumed).num from
          Int.add_nonneg (ih hrest) hc)

------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Lemma 24.3 – energy consumed after coreConsumeEnergy increases
------------------------------------------------------------------------
theorem coreConsumeEnergy_mono (c : ProcessingCore) (delta : Rat)
    (hpos : Rat.nonneg delta) (hcpos : Rat.nonneg c.energy_consumed) :
    Rat.nonneg (coreConsumeEnergy c delta hpos).energy_consumed :=
  show 0 ≤ (Rat.add c.energy_consumed delta).num from
    Int.add_nonneg hcpos hpos

------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- § 25  WEIGHT PROPAGATION DECAY INVARIANT
------------------------------------------------------------------------

def decayFactor (iteration : Nat) : Rat :=
  Nat.rec
    Rat.one
    (fun _ prev =>
      Rat.mul prev ⟨9, 10, by decide⟩)
    iteration

------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Lemma 25.1 – decayFactor 0 = 1
------------------------------------------------------------------------
theorem decayFactor_zero : decayFactor 0 = Rat.one :=
  Eq.refl _

------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Lemma 25.2 – decayFactor 1 = 9/10
------------------------------------------------------------------------
theorem decayFactor_one :
    (decayFactor 1).num = 9 ∧ (decayFactor 1).den = 10 :=
  And.intro (Eq.refl _) (Eq.refl _)

------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Lemma 25.3 – decayFactor is strictly positive (num > 0)
------------------------------------------------------------------------
theorem decayFactor_pos : ∀ n : Nat, 0 < (decayFactor n).num :=
  fun n =>
    Nat.rec
      (show (0 : Int) < 1 from Int.one_pos)
      (fun k ih =>
        show 0 < (Rat.mul (decayFactor k) ⟨9, 10, by decide⟩).num from
          show 0 < (decayFactor k).num * 9 from
            Int.mul_pos ih (by decide))
      n

------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Lemma 25.4 – applying decay k+1 times is product of decay k times and 9/10
------------------------------------------------------------------------
theorem decayFactor_succ (n : Nat) :
    decayFactor (n + 1) = Rat.mul (decayFactor n) ⟨9, 10, by decide⟩ :=
  Eq.refl _

------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Lemma 25.5 – denominator of decayFactor n = 10^n
------------------------------------------------------------------------
theorem decayFactor_den (n : Nat) :
    (decayFactor n).den = 10 ^ n := by
  induction n with
  | zero => simp [decayFactor, Rat.one]
  | succ k ih =>
    simp [decayFactor, Rat.mul, ih]
    ring

-- § 26  GRID TOPOLOGY INVARIANTS

def gridNeighbors (core_id gw gh : Nat) : List Nat :=
  let x := core_id % gw
  let y := core_id / gw
  let left  := if x > 0            then [core_id - 1]        else []
  let right := if x < gw - 1       then [core_id + 1]        else []
  let up    := if y > 0            then [core_id - gw]       else []
  let down  := if y < gh - 1       then [core_id + gw]       else []
  left ++ right ++ up ++ down

------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Lemma 26.1 – interior core has 4 neighbors
------------------------------------------------------------------------
theorem interior_core_4_neighbors (gw gh : Nat)
    (hgw : 2 < gw) (hgh : 2 < gh)
    (x y : Nat) (hx : 0 < x) (hx' : x < gw - 1)
    (hy : 0 < y) (hy' : y < gh - 1) :
    (gridNeighbors (y * gw + x) gw gh).length = 4 := by
  simp [gridNeighbors]
  have hmx  : (y * gw + x) % gw = x := by omega
  have hmy  : (y * gw + x) / gw = y := by omega
  simp [hmx, hmy, hx, hx', hy, hy']
  omega

------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Lemma 26.2 – corner core (0,0) has 2 neighbors in grid with gw,gh > 1
------------------------------------------------------------------------
theorem corner_00_2_neighbors (gw gh : Nat)
    (hgw : 1 < gw) (hgh : 1 < gh) :
    (gridNeighbors 0 gw gh).length = 2 := by
  simp [gridNeighbors]
  omega

------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Lemma 26.3 – gridNeighbors is always non-empty for valid 2x2+ grids
------------------------------------------------------------------------
theorem gridNeighbors_nonempty (cid gw gh : Nat)
    (hcid : cid < gw * gh) (hgw : 1 < gw) (hgh : 1 < gh) :
    0 < (gridNeighbors cid gw gh).length := by
  simp [gridNeighbors]
  omega

------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Lemma 26.4 – core_id = y * gw + x encodes coordinates
------------------------------------------------------------------------
theorem core_id_encodes (x y gw : Nat) (hx : x < gw) :
    (y * gw + x) % gw = x ∧ (y * gw + x) / gw = y :=
  And.intro (Nat.add_mul_mod_self_left x y gw ▸ Nat.mod_def x gw ▸ by omega)
            (by omega)

def routeLength (src_x src_y dst_x dst_y : Nat) : Nat :=
  let dx := if dst_x ≥ src_x then dst_x - src_x else src_x - dst_x
  let dy := if dst_y ≥ src_y then dst_y - src_y else src_y - dst_y
  dx + dy + 1

------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Lemma 27.1 – route from a point to itself has length 1
------------------------------------------------------------------------
theorem routeLength_self (x y : Nat) :
    routeLength x y x y = 1 :=
  Eq.refl _

------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Lemma 27.2 – routeLength is always ≥ 1
------------------------------------------------------------------------
theorem routeLength_pos (sx sy dx dy : Nat) :
    0 < routeLength sx sy dx dy :=
  Nat.lt_add_left _ _ _ (Nat.zero_lt_one)

------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Lemma 27.3 – routeLength is symmetric
------------------------------------------------------------------------
theorem routeLength_symm (sx sy dx dy : Nat) :
    routeLength sx sy dx dy = routeLength dx dy sx sy := by
  simp [routeLength]
  omega

------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Lemma 27.4 – Manhattan distance additivity (triangle inequality)
------------------------------------------------------------------------
theorem routeLength_triangle (x1 y1 x2 y2 x3 y3 : Nat) :
    routeLength x1 y1 x3 y3 ≤
      routeLength x1 y1 x2 y2 + routeLength x2 y2 x3 y3 - 1 := by
  simp [routeLength]
  omega

-- § 28  ISOMORPHISM SOUNDNESS: CANONICAL FORM PROPERTIES

def degreeSeqEquiv (g1 g2 : Graph) : Bool :=
  let ds1 := (g1.nodes.map (fun n =>
    (Graph.outDegree g1 n.id, Graph.inDegree g1 n.id))).mergeSort
      (fun a b => a.1 < b.1 || (a.1 == b.1 && a.2 ≤ b.2))
  let ds2 := (g2.nodes.map (fun n =>
    (Graph.outDegree g2 n.id, Graph.inDegree g2 n.id))).mergeSort
      (fun a b => a.1 < b.1 || (a.1 == b.1 && a.2 ≤ b.2))
  ds1.length == ds2.length &&
  (ds1.zipWith (fun a b => a == b) ds2).all id

------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Lemma 28.1 – degreeSeqEquiv is reflexive
------------------------------------------------------------------------
theorem degreeSeqEquiv_refl (g : Graph) :
    degreeSeqEquiv g g = true := by
  simp [degreeSeqEquiv, List.zipWith_self]
  simp [List.all_eq_true]
  intro x hx
  exact Nat.beq_refl x

------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Lemma 28.2 – different nodeCount implies not isomorphic
------------------------------------------------------------------------
theorem different_nodeCount_not_isomorphic (g1 g2 : Graph)
    (h : g1.nodeCount ≠ g2.nodeCount) :
    areIsomorphic g1 g2 = false := by
  simp [areIsomorphic, h]

------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Lemma 28.3 – single-node graphs with same qubit are isomorphic
------------------------------------------------------------------------
theorem single_node_isomorphic (n1 n2 : Node) (hq : n1.qubit = n2.qubit) :
    areIsomorphic (Graph.addNode Graph.empty n1)
                  (Graph.addNode Graph.empty n2) = true := by
  simp [areIsomorphic, Graph.nodeCount, Graph.edgeCount,
        graph_addNode_nodeCount, graph_addEdge_edgeCount]
  simp [CanonicalForm.beq, computeCanonicalForm]
  simp [Graph.outDegree, Graph.inDegree, Graph.empty]

def PowerSafety (pgc : PowerGatingController) : Prop :=
  Rat.le pgc.current_power pgc.power_budget

------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Lemma 29.1 – init satisfies PowerSafety
------------------------------------------------------------------------
theorem pgc_init_safety :
    PowerSafety PowerGatingController.init :=
  show Rat.le Rat.zero ⟨1000, 1, Nat.one_pos⟩ from
    show (0 : Int) * 1 ≤ 1000 * 1 from
      Int.zero_le_of_pos (by decide)

------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Lemma 29.2 – ungateCore preserves power budget when canUngate
------------------------------------------------------------------------
theorem pgc_ungate_budget_safe (pgc : PowerGatingController) (cid : Nat)
    (hg  : pgc.isGated cid = true)
    (hcan : pgc.canUngate = true)
    (hsafe : PowerSafety pgc) :
    PowerSafety (pgc.ungateCore cid).2 := by
  simp [PowerGatingController.ungateCore, hg, hcan]
  simp [PowerSafety, Rat.le, PowerGatingController.canUngate] at *
  exact hcan

------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- § 30  FULL SYSTEM CORRECTNESS: RPGU INVARIANT BUNDLE
------------------------------------------------------------------------

structure RPGUInvariant (rpgu : RelationalGraphProcessingUnit) : Prop where
  power_safe        : PowerSafety rpgu.power_gating
  exec_cycles_nat   : 0 ≤ rpgu.execution_cycles
  stats_coherent    :
    let s := rpgu.getStatistics
    s.active_cores + s.gated_cores = s.total_cores

------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Lemma 30.1 – init satisfies RPGUInvariant
------------------------------------------------------------------------
theorem rpgu_init_invariant (gw gh : Nat) :
    RPGUInvariant (RelationalGraphProcessingUnit.init gw gh) :=
  ⟨ pgc_init_safety
  , Nat.zero_le _
  , by
      simp [RPGUStatistics.safetyInvariant,
            RelationalGraphProcessingUnit.getStatistics,
            RelationalGraphProcessingUnit.init,
            AsynchronousNoC.init]
      rw [← List.length_append]
      congr 1
      rw [List.filter_append_not_filter] ⟩

------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Lemma 30.2 – setGlobalGraph preserves RPGUInvariant
------------------------------------------------------------------------
theorem rpgu_setGlobalGraph_preserves_inv
    (rpgu : RelationalGraphProcessingUnit)
    (g : Graph)
    (inv : RPGUInvariant rpgu) :
    RPGUInvariant (rpgu.setGlobalGraph g) :=
  ⟨ inv.power_safe
  , inv.exec_cycles_nat
  , by
      simp [RelationalGraphProcessingUnit.setGlobalGraph,
            RelationalGraphProcessingUnit.getStatistics]
      exact inv.stats_coherent ⟩

------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Lemma 30.3 – gating a core from RPGU preserves power safety
------------------------------------------------------------------------
theorem rpgu_gate_preserves_power_safety
    (rpgu : RelationalGraphProcessingUnit)
    (cid  : Nat)
    (hng  : rpgu.power_gating.isGated cid = false)
    (inv  : RPGUInvariant rpgu) :
    PowerSafety (rpgu.power_gating.gateCore cid).2 := by
  simp [PowerGatingController.gateCore,
        PowerGatingController.isGated, hng]
  simp [PowerSafety, Rat.le]
  -- Gating subtracts 10 from current_power, which makes it smaller,
  -- so if current_power ≤ budget, then current_power - 10 ≤ budget.
  have base := inv.power_safe
  simp [PowerSafety, Rat.le] at base
  linarith [base]
